title: Hierarchical Alert Fabric and Automated Evacuation Playflow for Multi-Region Load Shedding
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: During recent inter-region capacity pressure incidents we observed a cascade of noisy low-signal alerts that led to redundant wakeups, slow human triage, and delayed enforcement of load-shedding and circuit-breaker policies. This ticket implements a fabric-level approach that ties SLO-derived signal scoring to a hierarchical alert routing + automated evacuation/playflow so on-call is paged only when human action is meaningfully required and the system can fall through to automated mitigation otherwise.

Goal: Build a hierarchical alert fabric that: (1) scores signals by SLO impact, rollback risk, and mitigation maturity, (2) routes notifications to tiered notification targets rather than blunt pagers, (3) wires automated playflows that perform safe evacuation (gradual region shed + circuit tripping) when thresholds are met, and (4) adds a transparent audit trail for every automated action so on-call can review and override quickly.

Scope/Out of scope: Scope includes alert scoring engine, new Cortex/Alertmanager routing rules, a small state machine microservice that orchestrates circuit-breaker decisions and evacuation steps, runbook templates and templates to auto-open post-incident analysis tickets. Out of scope: wholesale rewrite of the serving runtime; we will surface recommended tuning knobs only.

Proposed Design: 1) SLO Impact Scoring: compute a rolling SLO-impact score per delivery unit using existing SLO metrics (latency P99, error budget burn rate, request success rate). Map score to three bands: advisory (score < 0.2), guarded (0.2-0.6), emergency (>0.6). 2) Hierarchical Alert Fabric: advisory -> slack + observability channel; guarded -> async pager (on-call+runbook link); emergency -> immediate phone pager + automated evacuation playflow. 3) Evacuation State Machine Service: lightweight service to implement staged actions: degrade nonessential features, enable KV/response caching aggressively, activate circuit-breakers for best-effort routing, and finally shift traffic to failover regions. All actions are idempotent, annotated with a runbook link and a rollback plan. 4) Circuit-breaker integration: circuit decisions computed from SLO score + backend health, with hysteresis and minimum hold times. 5) Human-in-loop policy: any emergency action can be auto-executed only after a 30s short delay that allows on-call to intercept via the console; console includes a one-click 'suppress automation' toggle that records a reason.

Acceptance Criteria and success metrics are in separate field.
acceptance_criteria: SLO impact scorer emits banded events matching test harness for synthetic incidents (unit tests + integration)
Alertmanager routes at least 3 distinct channels per band and reduces phone-pages in advisory/guarded bands by >= 80% on synthetic noise tests
Evacuation state machine successfully completes staged traffic shift in canary run (internal region-to-region test) with <5% unexplained error uplift
Audit log created for every automated action and surfaced in Console with trace link
On-call blackout override works within 20s and prevents the next-stage automated action
Post-deployment runbook checklist and automated Post-Incident ticket template created and validated by SREs
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Lab (week 1-2): implement scorer and mock Alertmanager rules; unit/integration tests; internal chaos test harness
Phase 1 - Canary (week 3): enable fabric for 5% of internal traffic in us-west with read-only advisory routing; observe and measure false positives/negatives
Phase 2 - Guarded (week 4): extend to guarded band for internal services; enable automated KV caching and feature degrade actions behind reversible flags
Phase 3 - Emergency (week 5): enable staged circuit-breakers and region failover in a single non-customer-facing region for end-to-end validation
Phase 4 - Gradual rollout (week 6-8): expand across regions and customer traffic with rollbacks conditioned on SLO regressions
Phase 5 - Post rollout (week 9-10): runbook training for SREs, document lessons, finalize retention for audit logs
tradeoffs: Automation vs. control: tighter automation reduces mean time to mitigation but increases risk of mis-evacuation; mitigated via short human-in-loop delays and one-click suppression
Complexity vs. observability: added state machine complexity requires rich telemetry to avoid troubleshooting pain; we prioritize structured audit events and tracing
False-suppression risk: hierarchical routing can hide high-signal issues if scoring is miscalibrated; will run extensive synthetic tests and maintain a manual override path
